text:
Tara R: FYI, we got an incident escalation from Support — multiple customers reporting p95/p99 spikes after the runtime v2.14.0 canary rollout ~20:02 UTC. Support ticket 8672. Looks like latency steadily rose at 20:05.
Miguel P: ack. I'm seeing a P99 jump from ~230ms to ~680ms on the canary pool in us-west-2. p95 also up. Checking the canary metrics now: https://grafana.redwood.example/d/abcd/runtime-latency?orgId=1 (link)
Ryan L: Deploy bot shows the canary rollout started at 19:58 and finished 20:03. Diff between v2.13.7 -> v2.14.0 includes kernel-selector changes + new batching heuristic.
Leah M: Can we pause/stop the rollout? If the canary is impacted we shouldn't promote.
Deploy Bot: Canaries: rollout completed to 2/5 hosts in us-west-2. Auto-promote disabled. /rollback not executed.
Miguel P: Did a quick query to trace logs:
```
trace_id=tx-9a8b sample: kernel_selector:chosen=kernel_v2_fast path=kvcache
latency_ms=682
```
Seems like the kernel selector is choosing kernel_v2_fast which under certain sequence lengths degenerates.
Ana S: I also see an increase in tail latencies in invocations with long context (>1024). Could be the kernel's attention tiling change.
Tara R: Support asked for mitigation while we triage. Any quick toggles? Maybe force old kernel per-model?
Ryan L: We can flip the kernel selector soft-switch via feature flag: `kernel.selector.force=legacy_v1` for canary pool. That should revert behaviour without full rollback. Recommend running on canary hosts first.
Miguel P: Doing that now on canary host id=can-03. Command:
```
kubectl exec can-03 -- /srv/runtime/bin/runtimectl set-feature kernel.selector.force=legacy_v1
```
Leah M: After the flip: p99 from 680 -> 245 within 90s on can-03. Other canaries still at high p99.
Tara R: Good signal — suggests kernel selector change is primary culprit. Let's run a binary bisect across the commits that touched kernel selector and batching.
Ryan L: I'm kicking off an automated bisect job; it will redeploy intermediate commits to two canary hosts and run load-checker against representative prompt set (promptset: ads-ranking-50k). Job id: bisect-2026-03-15-01. ETA ~18m.
SRE Bot: Bisect job started. Watch logs: https://ci.redwood.example/bisect-logs/bisect-2026-03-15-01
Miguel P: Parallelly collecting flamegraphs from can-03 with `perf` and `heaptrack` endpoints. Early stack samples show high time in `attention_dispatch::tile_loop` for kernel_v2_fast.
Ana S: Also seeing KV cache miss spikes during long-context requests after selector picks kernel_v2_fast — maybe cache policy mismatch.
Tara R: Any customers actively impacted? Support says enterprise-corp (cust-204) hit SLA alerts. Eng-sre oncall to open temporary SLA exception and notify AM.
Leah M: I've opened a slack thread with AMs and Support. Notifying cust-204 point of contact.
Ryan L: Bisect result: commit range narrowed to commit 9f3a2a -> 9f3a2d. Specifically 9f3a2c bumps batching heuristic threshold and defaults to kernel_v2_fast for seq>512.
Miguel P: Reproduced locally by running synthetic load with seq=1024 and batching set to aggressive: p99 ~700ms. Rebuilds with reverting the batching threshold drop resolves spike.
Ana S: Short-term mitigation: force legacy kernel on canary and schedule rollback of the batching-heuristic commit in the next patch release. Medium-term: add a presubmit perf test for seq distribution that exercises kernel_v2_fast paths.
Tara R: Action items:
- Miguel: push hotfix branch that reverts batching threshold (branch: hf/revert-batching-9f3a2c) and open PR. (ETA 1.5h)
- Ryan: coordinate rollback plan if hotfix can't be validated. (ETA 30m)
- Leah: keep Support/AMs updated; collect customer repro payloads. (ongoing)
- Ana: add a perf presubmit and a canary probe targeting long-context tails. (ETA 2d)
SRE Bot: Incident ticket created: INC-2026-1347. Linked to support ticket 8672.
Tara R: Miguel, once hotfix PR is ready, run canary deploy to the two affected canary hosts and validate latency using the real promptset.
Miguel P: PR open: https://git.redwood/example/pulls/4421. Running canary deploy to can-02 and can-03 now.
Leah M: Validation results: can-02 p99 dropped from 690->230; can-03 same. No errors in traces. Rolling out hotfix to remaining canaries paused until we get green from customers.
Ryan L: I'm drafting a postmortem note for product and execs summarizing root cause: batching heuristic + kernel selector combo caused tail latency regression for long-context workloads. Will include mitigations and rollout guard improvements.
Tara R: Thanks all. We'll keep this thread updated. If anyone finds additional signal (other regions/models) paste here. :thumbsup:
